```{python}
#| label: setup

import os
from pathlib import Path

from IPython.display import display

from lortrace.benchmark import report as R

REPO = next(p for p in (Path.cwd(), *Path.cwd().parents) if (p / "pyproject.toml").is_file())
# Released results by default; point RESULTS_DIR at a reproduced run,
# e.g. RESULTS_DIR=outputs/rescore quarto render report/results.qmd
RESULTS_REL = os.environ.get("RESULTS_DIR", "results")
MODELS = R.load_models(REPO / RESULTS_REL, REPO / "weights")
C = R.cohort(MODELS)
BASE = C["forecast_recall"]

best_auc = max(MODELS, key=R.roc_auc)
best_q90 = max(MODELS, key=lambda m: R.at_q(m, "q90", "recall"))
beat_q90 = [m["label"] for m in MODELS if R.at_q(m, "q90", "recall") > BASE]


def show(df, digits=3):
    num = [c for c in df.columns if df[c].dtype.kind == "f"]
    return df.style.format({c: f"{{:.{digits}f}}" for c in num}, na_rep="—").hide(axis="index")
```

# Overview

Unsupervised backbone sweep on NSW1 five-minute market windows under one matched
contract: train-only scaling, \(W{=}H{=}12\) windows, unsupervised LoRA
fine-tuning, value-token negative log-likelihood (NLL) scoring, Actual
Lack-of-Reserve (LOR) as ground truth, and AEMO Forecast LOR as a threshold-free
institutional baseline. Everything below is computed from `results/<model>/`
(override with `RESULTS_DIR`); models are ordered by nominal size.

```{python}
print(
    f"{C['n_models']} backbones under {RESULTS_REL}/. Evaluation pool: {C['n_eval']:,} "
    f"windows; Actual LOR: {C['n_pos']} ({100 * C['prevalence']:.2f}%). "
    f"Forecast LOR recall = {BASE:.3f}."
)
```

::: {.callout-important}
Actual LOR windows are rarer than 1%, so **accuracy is not informative**. We report
**ROC-AUC** (ranking), **recall at score quantiles** \(q\in\{0.90,0.95,0.99\}\) and
severity-specific recall. LOR3 recall is undefined because no Actual LOR3 window
occurs in the evaluation period.
:::

# Ranking and operating-point recall

```{python}
#| label: tbl-ranking
#| tbl-cap: "ROC-AUC, average precision and recall at q90/q95/q99; last column is q90 recall minus Forecast LOR recall."
show(R.table_ranking(MODELS))
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-roc-auc
#| fig-cap: "ROC-AUC of value-token NLL scores against Actual LOR. The dotted line marks chance (0.5)."
display(R.fig_roc_auc(MODELS))
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-recall-quantiles
#| fig-cap: "Actual-LOR recall at model-specific score quantiles. The dashed line is the threshold-free Forecast LOR recall."
display(R.fig_recall_quantiles(MODELS))
```

All backbones rank Actual LOR windows above chance, but AUC stays moderate. The best
ranking is **`{python} best_auc["label"]`** (ROC-AUC
`{python} f"{R.roc_auc(best_auc):.3f}"`). At \(q{=}0.90\) the best coverage is
**`{python} best_q90["label"]`** (recall
`{python} f"{R.at_q(best_q90, 'q90', 'recall'):.3f}"` vs Forecast LOR
`{python} f"{BASE:.3f}"`); backbones above the baseline at \(q{=}0.90\):
`{python} ", ".join(beat_q90) or "none"`. Recall falls sharply at stricter quantiles.

# Precision, F1 and false-positive rate

```{python}
#| label: tbl-precision-f1
#| tbl-cap: "Precision, F1 and false-positive rate at each quantile (Actual LOR ground truth)."
show(R.table_precision_f1(MODELS), 4)
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-precision-recall-q90
#| fig-cap: "Precision vs recall at q90. The dashed line is Forecast LOR recall."
display(R.fig_precision_recall_q90(MODELS))
```

Precision is low at every quantile because even a 1–10% alarm rate far exceeds the
~1% prevalence. FPR tracks the nominal rate (\(\approx 0.10/0.05/0.01\)) by
construction, so models differ mainly in *which* rare windows they capture.

# Severity-specific recall

```{python}
#| label: tbl-severity
#| tbl-cap: "Per-severity Actual LOR recall at q90 and q95 (— = no windows of that severity, or not applicable)."
show(R.table_severity(MODELS))
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-severity-q90
#| fig-cap: "Per-severity Actual LOR recall at q90. Dashed lines mark Forecast LOR recall for each severity."
display(R.fig_severity_q90(MODELS))
```

Overall recall can hide very different LOR1/LOR2 mixes; reporting both avoids
mistaking a LOR1-only detector for broad reserve-stress coverage.

# Score distributions

```{python}
#| label: fig-score-distributions
#| fig-cap: "Per-model score distributions on val∪test. Grey: non-LOR; orange: Actual LOR. Lines mark the q90 / q95 / q99 thresholds."
#| fig-height: 12
display(R.fig_score_distributions(MODELS))
```

Actual LOR windows sit to the right but overlap heavily with the bulk, consistent
with moderate AUC. Absolute NLL scales differ across tokenizers, which is why
thresholds are model-specific quantiles.
